items.title: 6.7 Enthalpy change and calorie content of food

blocks.text: Foods can be looked at as fuels. When food is digested, the chemical energy stored in it, also called its calorie content, is released as heat; digestion releases the same amount of energy as burning the food outside the body, so the overall enthalpy of combustion is the same as the heat of combustion, which can be determined in a calorimeter, typically a bomb calorimeter.

blocks.title: Calorie content
blocks.text: The calorie content of a food is a measure of the energy released when the food is completely consumed in the body, typically expressed in kilocalories (kcal) or joules (J).

blocks.prompt: Why can the energy a body gets from a spoon of sugar be measured by burning the sugar in a calorimeter?
blocks.explanation: By Hess's law the enthalpy change from sugar and oxygen to carbon dioxide and water is the same whatever the route. Digestion and burning start and end with the same substances, so they release the same energy, and the calorimeter's heat of combustion equals the body's calorie content.

items: Food is a fuel: digestion releases the same energy as combustion, measured in a (bomb) calorimeter; calorie content is that energy in kcal or J.
